Text: “We were out on maneuvers”, {d(Finder)} reports, “when we discerned a large object on our sensors”

“We did not realise just how large...”

The visual feed switches to a ship, but one larger than you’ve ever flown in. It must be pre-Collapse, but you had no idea they built ships this size...

“As you know,” quips {d(Finder)}, “I am entitled to half its value, as the discoverer - but I would prefer to study the entire ship."

Your teams pick the titan clean

The ship originally carried fighters and interceptors within its bulk: a floating spaceport. Your technicians report a number of references to the pre-Collapse League of Spacefaring Nations: insignias, watermarks, the medals of the dead. She must have been a League warship.

“She was wrecked when the sun went nova,” explains the lead tech. “They tried to outrun it, but even a giant can be felled.”

“We've picked her clean, my {Up(title(PlayerCharacter))}. What should we do with her?”
We lack the means to refit her. Scrap her instead

The vessel will be towed to your home system; once repaired, it can be used as living space.
The giant stirs

Not by her own efforts - you have your towing fleet to thank for that - but she stirs, nonetheless. In a few weeks you ease her into a stable orbit, and welcome families on board.

You're unsure how the League would feel to see thousands of common folk camped out against its bulkheads and hatchways. If repaired, this living space could house thousands of your people.
Prepared to repurpose derelict warship
{D_s(Ruler)} technicians have accessed the titanic ship's data stores
The ship’s logs shed some light on how the vessel came to be.

The ISS Athena was a joint project between five nation states, which together formed the League of Spacefaring Nations. None could have accomplished this alone: they joined forces to construct a carrier not only for mutual defence against their rivals, but to preserve their shared values.
If they could band together, perhaps we can too
The galaxy learns of the League's accomplishment
